claim: Emerging hair progenitors produce both WNTs and WNT inhibitors.
source: Coupling transcriptomics with genetics, we show that emerging hair progenitors produce both WNTs and WNT inhibitors.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding, which is supported by transcriptomic data presented in the manuscript (Figure 2, Figure 3).

claim: WNT activators and inhibitors oppositely polarize in hair progenitors instead of generating a negative feedback loop.
source: Surprisingly, however, instead of generating a negative feedback loop, the signals oppositely polarize, establishing sharp boundaries and consequently a short-range morphogen gradient that we show is essential for three-dimensional pattern formation.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by immunofluorescence data showing differential localization of WNT ligands and inhibitors (Figure 4, Figure 5).

claim: The morphogen gradient established by opposite polarization is essential for three-dimensional pattern formation.
source: Surprisingly, however, instead of generating a negative feedback loop, the signals oppositely polarize, establishing sharp boundaries and consequently a short-range morphogen gradient that we show is essential for three-dimensional pattern formation.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by functional experiments showing disrupted hair follicle morphogenesis when the gradient is perturbed (Figure 6).

claim: The progenitor preserves its WNT signaling identity while its overlying epithelial cells become WNT-restricted.
source: The progenitor preserves its WNT signaling identity and maintains WNT signaling with underlying mesenchymal neighbors, while its overlying epithelial cells become WNT-restricted.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by immunofluorescence data showing differential WNT signaling in basal versus suprabasal cells (Figure 1A, Figure 4).

claim: The progenitor maintains WNT signaling with underlying mesenchymal neighbors.
source: The progenitor preserves its WNT signaling identity and maintains WNT signaling with underlying mesenchymal neighbors, while its overlying epithelial cells become WNT-restricted.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by immunofluorescence data showing WNT signaling in the dermal condensate (Figure 1A, Figure 4).

claim: Nuclear LEF1 co-localizes with nuclear β-catenin in the skin.
source: In the skin, it is well-established that nuclear LEF1 co-localizes not only with nuclear β-catenin (Fuchs et al., 2001) but also with both TOPGAL, a WNT-reporter driven by an enhancer composed of multimerized LEF1 DNA binding sites (DasGupta and Fuchs, 1999), and as shown in Figure 1A, Axin2-LacZ, a WNT-reporter driven by the endogenous WNT target Axin2 (Lustig et al., 2002).
evidence: The text cites previous literature (Fuchs et al., 2001) to support this claim.

claim: Nuclear LEF1 co-localizes with TOPGAL, a WNT-reporter driven by an enhancer composed of multimerized LEF1 DNA binding sites.
source: In the skin, it is well-established that nuclear LEF1 co-localizes not only with nuclear β-catenin (Fuchs et al., 2001) but also with both TOPGAL, a WNT-reporter driven by an enhancer composed of multimerized LEF1 DNA binding sites (DasGupta and Fuchs, 1999), and as shown in Figure 1A, Axin2-LacZ, a WNT-reporter driven by the endogenous WNT target Axin2 (Lustig et al., 2002).
evidence: The text cites previous literature (DasGupta and Fuchs, 1999) to support this claim.

claim: Nuclear LEF1 co-localizes with Axin2-LacZ, a WNT-reporter driven by the endogenous WNT target Axin2.
source: In the skin, it is well-established that nuclear LEF1 co-localizes not only with nuclear β-catenin (Fuchs et al., 2001) but also with both TOPGAL, a WNT-reporter driven by an enhancer composed of multimerized LEF1 DNA binding sites (DasGupta and Fuchs, 1999), and as shown in Figure 1A, Axin2-LacZ, a WNT-reporter driven by the endogenous WNT target Axin2 (Lustig et al., 2002).
evidence: The text cites previous literature (Lustig et al., 2002) and references Figure 1A showing co-localization.

claim: Mosaic loss of Apc results in overactivation of β-catenin/WNT signaling in patches of transduced skin.
source: As expected from prior Apc loss of function studies on E14.5 embryos (Kuraguchi et al., 2006), mosaic loss of Apc resulted in overactivation of β-catenin/WNT signaling in patches of transduced skin (Figure 1B).
evidence: The text cites previous literature (Kuraguchi et al., 2006) and references Figure 1B showing the experimental result.

claim: Hair follicle patterning was severely perturbed upon mosaic, autonomous over-stabilization of β-catenin.
source: In contrast to wild-type and/or Apc-/+ skin, where waves of LEF1+ placodes were patterned equidistantly in hexagonal arrays (Zhou et al., 1995; Cheng et al., 2014), hair follicle patterning was severely perturbed upon mosaic, autonomous over-stabilization of β-catenin (Figure 1C–E).
evidence: The text cites previous literature (Zhou et al., 1995; Cheng et al., 2014) and references Figure 1C-E showing the experimental result.

claim: Apc-null clusters displayed intense nuclear β-catenin and nuclear LEF1.
source: While immunostaining revealed intense nuclear β-catenin as well as nuclear LEF1, Apc-null clusters were of random sizes and organization and the clusters never developed into bona fide hair buds.
evidence: The text describes immunostaining results showing intense nuclear β-catenin and LEF1 in Apc-null clusters.

claim: Apc-null clusters were of random sizes and organization.
source: While immunostaining revealed intense nuclear β-catenin as well as nuclear LEF1, Apc-null clusters were of random sizes and organization and the clusters never developed into bona fide hair buds.
evidence: The text describes the morphological characteristics of Apc-null clusters.

claim: Apc-null clusters never developed into bona fide hair buds.
source: While immunostaining revealed intense nuclear β-catenin as well as nuclear LEF1, Apc-null clusters were of random sizes and organization and the clusters never developed into bona fide hair buds.
evidence: The text describes the developmental outcome of Apc-null clusters.

claim: Apc-null clusters remained uniform for the natural markers of WNThi placode cells LEF1, β-catenin and Lhx2.
source: Instead, clusters remained uniform for the natural markers of WNThi placode cells LEF1, β-catenin and Lhx2, but they failed to generate the WNTlo suprabasal cells that characterize the placode to hair bud transition (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: The text describes marker expression in Apc-null clusters and references Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–C.

claim: Apc-null clusters failed to generate the WNTlo suprabasal cells that characterize the placode to hair bud transition.
source: Instead, clusters remained uniform for the natural markers of WNThi placode cells LEF1, β-catenin and Lhx2, but they failed to generate the WNTlo suprabasal cells that characterize the placode to hair bud transition (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: The text describes the absence of WNTlo suprabasal cells in Apc-null clusters and references Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–C.

claim: No signs of DNA damage were observed in Apc-null clusters as judged by the absence of γH2AX signal.
source: No signs of DNA damage were observed in Apc-null clusters as judged by the absence of γH2AX signal (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–B).
evidence: The text describes the absence of DNA damage markers and references Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–B.

claim: Apc-null clusters appeared to be altogether non-proliferative.
source: Although wild-type WNThi hair bud cells are slow-cycling (Ouspenskaia et al., 2016), Apc-null clusters appeared to be altogether non-proliferative (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A–B).
evidence: The text cites previous literature (Ouspenskaia et al., 2016) and references Figure 1—figure supplement 3A–B showing proliferation data.

claim: Both wild-type placodes and Apc-null clusters were multiclonal.
source: Moreover, as illuminated by co-transducing E9.5 embryos with GFP- and RFP-tagged Cre recombinase-expressing lentiviruses, both wild-type placodes and Apc-null clusters were multiclonal (Figure 1—figure supplement 3C), in agreement with the notion that WNT drives the organization of non-dividing cells into placodes within the epidermal plane (Ahtiainen et al., 2014).
evidence: The text describes the experimental result and references Figure 1—figure supplement 3C, also citing previous literature (Ahtiainen et al., 2014).

claim: The distinct morphology of Apc-null clusters within the epidermis was characterized by a loss of E-cadherin but not P-cadherin.
source: The distinct morphology of Apc-null clusters within the epidermis was characterized by a loss of E-cadherin but not P-cadherin (Figure 1—figure supplement 4A–B), suggestive of a collective cell sorting mechanism dependent on sustained WNT activation.
evidence: The text describes the immunofluorescence results and references Figure 1—figure supplement 4A–B.

claim: Integrin β4 was markedly reduced in Apc-null clusters, consistent with an overall loss of polarity in these clusters.
source: Integrin β4 was also markedly reduced, consistent with an overall loss of polarity in these clusters (Figure 1—figure supplement 5A–B).
evidence: The text describes the immunofluorescence results and references Figure 1—figure supplement 5A–B.

claim: The WNTlo (LEF1-negative) regions surrounding Apc-null clusters occupied a much greater than normal radius.
source: Finally, the WNTlo (LEF1-negative) regions surrounding Apc-null clusters occupied a much greater than normal radius (Figure 1C).
evidence: The text describes the observation and references Figure 1C.

claim: When WNT signaling becomes too high, neighboring cells become too low for WNT signaling, sharpening the boundary between WNThi and WNTlo cells and disrupting hair follicle patterning.
source: Taken together, our mosaic data revealed that when WNT signaling becomes too high, neighboring cells become too low for WNT signaling, sharpening the boundary between WNThi and WNTlo cells and disrupting hair follicle patterning.
evidence: The text summarizes the findings from the mosaic Apc-null experiments.

claim: WNT-reporterhi epidermal progenitors that were null for Apc displayed robust upregulation of established WNT-target genes.
source: When compared to their heterozygous counterparts, WNT-reporterhi epidermal progenitors (α6 integrin+) that were null for Apc, displayed robust upregulation (Log2 Fold Change ≥ 1.5, p<0.05) of established WNT-target genes, for example Axin2, Twist1/2 and Bmp4, as well as transcripts associated with WNT signaling, cell-cell signaling, cancer, epithelial-mesenchymal transition and cell adhesion (Figure 2B–D and Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The text describes the RNA-seq results and references Figure 2B–D and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: WNT signaling sensitive genes encoded not only WNT-activators but also WNT-inhibitors, including NOTUM, WIF1, DKK4 and APCDD1.
source: Intriguingly, WNT signaling sensitive genes encoded not only WNT-activators but also WNT-inhibitors, including NOTUM, WIF1, DKK4 and APCDD1.
evidence: The text describes the RNA-seq results identifying WNT inhibitors as WNT-sensitive genes.

claim: The levels of WNT target gene expression were always higher in Apc-null than in non-phenotypic Apc-heterozygous cells.
source: Notably, the levels of WNT target gene expression were always higher in Apc-null than in non-phenotypic Apc-heterozygous cells, consistent with their overall ectopically higher levels of β-catenin (Figure 2D).
evidence: The text describes the RNA-seq results and references Figure 2D.

claim: Wild-type basal hair bud progenitors share strong signature similarities with Apc-null progenitors.
source: Indeed, not only was this wild-type population WNT-reporter active (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), but in addition, the transcriptome overlapped appreciably with that of the WNThi potent Apc-null cells (Figure 3B; Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The text describes the RNA-seq comparison and references Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: WNT signaling activators and inhibitors fell within the overlap between Apc-null WNThi and wild-type WNThi transcriptomes.
source: Most notably, WNT signaling activators and inhibitors fell within the overlap (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The text describes the RNA-seq comparison and references Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Many WNT signaling factors displayed expression specificity for the WNThi and not WNTlo cells of wild-type epithelial cells.
source: As confirmed by in situ hybridization, many of these factors displayed expression specificity for the WNThi and not WNTlo cells of wild-type epithelial cells (Figure 3C).
evidence: The text describes the in situ hybridization results and references Figure 3C.

claim: Bmp4 was among the genes exhibiting strong WNT signaling dependency.
source: Bmp4 was among the genes exhibiting strong WNT signaling dependency (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A–C).
evidence: The text describes the RNA-seq and immunofluorescence results and references Figure 3—figure supplement 3A–C.

claim: Nuclear pSMAD1/5/9 persisted multiple cell layers away from Apc-null clusters.
source: Indeed, nuclear pSMAD1/5/9, a proxy for BMP4 signaling, persisted multiple cell layers away from Apc-null clusters (Figure 3—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: The text describes the immunofluorescence results and references Figure 3—figure supplement 3C.

claim: When over-expressed mosaically, BMP suppressed hair bud formation within adjacent regions of wild-type skin, accompanied by aberrant expansion of pSMAD1/5/9.
source: Moreover, when over-expressed mosaically, BMP suppressed hair bud formation within adjacent regions of wild-type skin, accompanied by aberrant expansion of pSMAD1/5/9 (Figure 3—figure supplement 3D–G).
evidence: The text describes the experimental results and references Figure 3—figure supplement 3D–G.

claim: BMP4 acts in a long-range, negative feedback loop and is responsible for creating a bud-free environment around WNT-specified hair buds.
source: These findings support the notion that BMP4 acts in a long-range, negative feedback loop and is responsible for creating a bud-free environment around WNT-specified hair buds, which are driven by BMP inhibitors.
evidence: The text summarizes the findings from the BMP experiments.

claim: WNTs seemed to function locally, since despite marked elevation of WNT10B within Apc-null clusters, immunostaining did not reveal signs of long-range expansion of nuclear β-catenin/LEF1 or WNT inhibitors into surrounding wild-type skin.
source: By contrast, and as previously reported for intestine (Farin et al., 2016), WNTs seemed to function locally, since despite marked elevation of WNT10B within Apc-null clusters, immunostaining did not reveal signs of long-range expansion of nuclear β-catenin/LEF1 or WNT inhibitors (NOTUM and WIF1) into surrounding wild-type skin (Figure 3—figure supplement 4A and B).
evidence: The text describes the immunofluorescence results, cites previous literature (Farin et al., 2016), and references Figure 3—figure supplement 4A and B.

claim: WIF1 localized at the apical side of the basal cells of placode, bud and germs.
source: Strikingly, WIF1 localized at the apical side of the basal cells of placode, bud and germs (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: The text describes the immunofluorescence results and references Figure 4A and B.

claim: WIF1's apical localization in hair germs was severely impaired by Tunicamycin, suggestive of a role for N-Glycosylation in the preferential apical secretion of WNT inhibitors.
source: WIF1's apical localization in hair germs was severely impaired by Tunicamycin, suggestive of a role for N-Glycosylation in the preferential apical secretion of WNT inhibitors (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A; Scheiffele et al., 1995).
evidence: The text describes the experimental results, cites previous literature (Scheiffele et al., 1995), and references Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Endogenous NOTUM displayed a marked apical localization in basal bud cells.
source: Like WIF1, endogenous NOTUM also displayed a marked apical localization in basal bud cells (Figure 4C).
evidence: The text describes the immunofluorescence results and references Figure 4C.

claim: Nuclear LEF1 was drastically reduced in the suprabasal bud cells at the interface of the high zone of WNT-inhibitor.
source: Moreover, consistent with WIF1's role in binding and trapping WNT ligands (Malinauskas et al., 2011), and NOTUM's role in inactivating secreted WNTs through removal of their palmitoleate moiety (Kakugawa et al., 2015), nuclear LEF1 was drastically reduced in the suprabasal bud cells at the interface of this high zone of WNT-inhibitor (Figure 4B and C; white arrows).
evidence: The text describes the immunofluorescence results, cites previous literature (Malinauskas et al., 2011; Kakugawa et al., 2015), and references Figure 4B and C.

claim: By the hair germ stage, WIF1 was no longer expressed in the dermal condensate.
source: By the hair germ stage, WIF1 was no longer expressed in the dermal condensate (Figure 4B; Figure 5B; Figure 5—figure supplement 1B), nor was NOTUM at the dermal condensate-epidermal interface (Figure 4C; Figure 5C; Figure 5—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: The text describes the immunofluorescence results and references multiple figures.

claim: By the hair germ stage, NOTUM was no longer expressed at the dermal condensate-epidermal interface.
source: By the hair germ stage, WIF1 was no longer expressed in the dermal condensate (Figure 4B; Figure 5B; Figure 5—figure supplement 1B), nor was NOTUM at the dermal condensate-epidermal interface (Figure 4C; Figure 5C; Figure 5—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: The text describes the immunofluorescence results and references multiple figures.

claim: By polarizing WNT-inhibitors apically in basal hair bud cells, a WNT-inhibitor free zone appeared to be generated at the epithelial-mesenchymal interface.
source: Thus, by polarizing WNT-inhibitors apically in basal hair bud cells, a WNT-inhibitor free zone appeared to be generated at this epithelial-mesenchymal interface (yellow arrowheads, Figure 4B and C).
evidence: The text describes the inference from immunofluorescence results and references Figure 4B and C.

claim: The robust presence of nuclear LEF1 both in basal bud cells and in the dermal condensate suggested the presence of active WNT ligands within the inhibitor-free zone.
source: Moreover, the robust presence of nuclear LEF1 both in basal bud cells and in the dermal condensate suggested the presence of active WNT ligands within this inhibitor-free zone.
evidence: The text describes the inference from immunofluorescence results.

claim: WNT10B and WNT3 were both preferentially polarized at the basal membrane.
source: Indeed, in contrast to WNT inhibitors, WNT10B and WNT3 were both preferentially polarized at the basal membrane, as quantified by pixel intensity analyses (Figure 5D; Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The text describes the immunofluorescence results and references Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claim: Frizzled-10 WNT receptor localized to all borders of the hair germ progenitor cells.
source: In contrast to the polarization of WNT ligands and WNT inhibitors, Frizzled-10 WNT receptor localized to all borders of the hair germ progenitor cells (Figure 5E).
evidence: The text describes the immunofluorescence results and references Figure 5E.

claim: Elevating WNT inhibitors impaired hair follicle specification and led to a sparser hair coat.
source: In doing so, we observed that WNT inhibitors impaired hair follicle specification and led to a sparser hair coat (Figure 6A; Figure 6—figure supplement 1A and B–B').
evidence: The text describes the experimental results and references Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A and B–B'.

claim: Low doses of LGK974 administered to E15.5 skin explants were sufficient to prevent nuclear LEF1 in the normally WNThi basal hair bud cells.
source: Low doses of LGK974 administered to E15.5 skin explants were sufficient to prevent nuclear LEF1 in the normally WNThi basal hair bud cells.
evidence: The text describes the experimental results from LGK974 treatment.

claim: Low doses of LGK974 caused the normally WNThi basal cells to adopt the SOX9 fate of the WNTlo suprabasal bud cells.
source: Moreover, the normally WNThi basal cells adopted the SOX9 fate of the WNTlo suprabasal bud cells, underscoring the importance of the WNT morphogen gradient in fate specification (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: The text describes the experimental results and references Figure 6—figure supplement 2A–C.

claim: At higher doses of LGK974, LEF1 was lost not only from the basal hair bud cells, but also from the dermal condensates.
source: At higher doses, LEF1 was lost not only from the basal hair bud cells, but also from the dermal condensates, consistent with the higher levels of nuclear LEF1/WNT signaling in the dermal condensate relative to the hair bud (Figure 6—figure supplement 2D and E).
evidence: The text describes the experimental results and references Figure 6—figure supplement 2D and E.

claim: When the low dose porcupine inhibitor was washed out, nuclear LEF1 and basal bud progenitor fate was restored.
source: Moreover, when we washed out the low dose porcupine inhibitor, nuclear LEF1 and basal bud progenitor fate was restored, illustrating not only the reversibility of the process, but also the restriction of WNT signaling to the epithelial-dermal condensate boundary (Figure 6—figure supplement 3A and B).
evidence: The text describes the experimental results and references Figure 6—figure supplement 3A and B.

claim: In the basal cells from the developing hair follicle, LEF1 perfectly co-localized with TCF1/7, the nuclear effector of WNT signaling.
source: In the basal cells from the developing hair follicle LEF1 perfectly co-localized with TCF1/7, the nuclear effector of WNT signaling.
evidence: The text describes the immunofluorescence results.

claim: WNT-reporterhi, LEF1 positive progenitor cells co-expressed other key WNT signaling pathway components like FZD10 and WIF1.
source: Furthermore WNT-reporterhi, LEF1 positive progenitor cells co-expressed other key WNT signaling pathway components like FZD10 and WIF1 (Figure 6—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The text describes the immunofluorescence results and references Figure 6—figure supplement 4.

claim: Basal targeting of AQP4-tagged WNT-inhibitors was more efficient with NOTUM, and this correlated with a more pronounced reduction in hair follicles.
source: Quantifications showed that basal targeting was more efficient with NOTUM, and this correlated with a more pronounced reduction in hair follicles.
evidence: The text describes the quantification results from the AQP4-tagging experiments.

claim: The nuclear LEF1 signal was significantly decreased in NOTUM-AQP4-induced cells compared to either NOTUM-induced or wild-type cells.
source: Moreover, as quantified by nuclear LEF1 fluorescence intensity, the nuclear LEF1 signal was significantly decreased in NOTUM-AQP4-induced cells compared to either NOTUM-induced or wild-type cells (Figure 6C).
evidence: The text describes the quantification results and references Figure 6C.

claim: Mispolarization of NOTUM resulted in an expansion of WNTlo SOX9 cells.
source: These manipulations also resulted in an expansion of WNTlo SOX9 cells, underlying the importance of properly regulating WNT inhibitors in hair follicle morphogenesis (Figure 6D).
evidence: The text describes the experimental results and references Figure 6D.

claim: In the absence of NOTUM, both the proportion of LEF1+ cells and also their nuclear LEF1 signal intensity were significantly increased within developing hair buds.
source: By transducing Notum fl/fl and Notumfl/+ R26td Tomato embryos with LV-Cre, we found that in the absence of NOTUM, both the proportion of LEF1+ cells and also their nuclear LEF1 signal intensity were significantly increased within developing hair buds (Figure 7A–C).
evidence: The text describes the experimental results and references Figure 7A–C.

claim: The effects of Notum ablation were largely confined to the apical region of the hair bud and not the underlying dermal condensate.
source: Moreover, the effects of Notum ablation were largely confined to the apical region of the hair bud and not the underlying dermal condensate, further underscoring the short range and functional importance of apically localizing WNT inhibitors.
evidence: The text describes the experimental results from Notum ablation.

claim: By differentially compartmentalizing WNTs and WNT inhibitors, basal placode progenitors maintain both positive and negative WNT morphogens simultaneously.
source: Our findings show that by differentially compartmentalizing WNTs and WNT inhibitors, basal placode progenitors not only maintain both positive and negative WNT morphogens simultaneously, but also directionally target the signals, providing the requisite positional cues to transition from two to three dimensional patterning within the developing tissue.
evidence: The text summarizes the main findings of the study.

claim: By polarizing WNTs basally, progenitors are able to retain their own WNT signaling as well as that of their underlying mesenchymal neighbors to fuel hair follicle morphogenesis at the dermal-epidermal interface.
source: By polarizing WNTs basally, progenitors are able to retain their own WNT signaling as well as that of their underlying mesenchymal neighbors to fuel hair follicle morphogenesis at the dermal-epidermal interface.
evidence: The text summarizes the main findings of the study.

claim: By polarizing WNT inhibitors apically, the same hair bud progenitors directionally orchestrate WNTloSOX9+ fate specification of their overlying neighbors to launch the diversification of the epithelial cells within the developing hair follicles.
source: Conversely, by polarizing WNT inhibitors apically, the same hair bud progenitors directionally orchestrate WNTloSOX9+ fate specification of their overlying neighbors to launch the diversification of the epithelial cells within the developing hair follicles (Figure 8).
evidence: The text summarizes the main findings of the study and references Figure 8.

claim: Developing hair follicle progenitors use WNTs and WNT inhibitors to build local boundaries.
source: Our findings best fit a model whereby developing hair follicle progenitors use WNTs and WNT inhibitors to build local boundaries.
evidence: The text summarizes the interpretation of the findings.

claim: By localizing WNT inhibitors apically, WNThigh progenitors limit the WNT response, preserving their own WNThigh signaling identity while simultaneously preventing their suprabasal daughter from responding to the WNT signal.
source: By localizing WNT inhibitors apically, WNThigh progenitors limit the WNT response, preserving their own WNThigh signaling identity while simultaneously preventing their suprabasal daughter from responding to the WNT signal.
evidence: The text summarizes the interpretation of the findings.

claim: In Drosophila imaginal disks, cells that are closer to the dorsoventral boundary are able to repress wingless expression in their juxtaposed neighbors through a self-refining mechanism involving NOTCH.
source: A similar refining mechanism has been previously proposed in the Drosophila imaginal disks. In the wingless expressing cells of the wing margin, cells that are closer to the dorsoventral boundary are able to repress wingless expression in their juxtaposed neighbors through a self-refining mechanism. In this case, however, the mechanism appears to involve NOTCH, whose activity is required for wingless expression, which in turn appears to repress NOTCH activity (Rulifson et al., 1996).
evidence: The text cites previous literature (Rulifson et al., 1996) to support this claim.

claim: In the hair follicle, NOTCH signaling has not been detected in the WNT10B+ progenitors, but rather the WNTlow differentiating cells.
source: In the hair follicle, NOTCH signaling has not been detected in the WNT10B+ progenitors, but rather the WNTlow differentiating cells (Blanpain et al., 2006).
evidence: The text cites previous literature (Blanpain et al., 2006) to support this claim.

claim: WNTs are known to be N-glycosylated.
source: WNTs are known to be N-glycosylated, and studies in Drosophila suggest that WNTs can be secreted apically and then transported basally (Yamazaki et al., 2016).
evidence: The text cites previous literature (Yamazaki et al., 2016) to support this claim.

claim: In Drosophila, N-glycosylation-deficient Wingless is secreted without consequence.
source: Intriguingly, however, in Drosophila, N-glycosylation-deficient Wingless is secreted without consequence (Tang et al., 2012), and in mammalian cells, WNTs have been found to be more potent and bind extracellular matrix more robustly in the absence of N-glycosylation (Doubravska et al., 2011).
evidence: The text cites previous literature (Tang et al., 2012) to support this claim.

claim: In mammalian cells, WNTs have been found to be more potent and bind extracellular matrix more robustly in the absence of N-glycosylation.
source: Intriguingly, however, in Drosophila, N-glycosylation-deficient Wingless is secreted without consequence (Tang et al., 2012), and in mammalian cells, WNTs have been found to be more potent and bind extracellular matrix more robustly in the absence of N-glycosylation (Doubravska et al., 2011).
evidence: The text cites previous literature (Doubravska et al., 2011) to support this claim.

claim: The ability of ECM to retain growth factors, including WNT regulators, makes it advantageous for cells such as hair bud progenitors that adhere to a basement membrane to secrete their WNTs basally.
source: The ability of ECM to retain growth factors (Baeg et al., 2001), including WNT regulators, makes this hypothesis all the more attractive.
evidence: The text cites previous literature (Baeg et al., 2001) and provides speculation about the mechanism.

claim: By establishing a morphogen gradient at the cellular level, signals are constrained such that two neighboring cell populations in direct physical contact can effectively receive different signaling inputs.
source: In closing, by establishing a morphogen gradient at the cellular level, signals are constrained such that two neighboring cell populations in direct physical contact can effectively receive different signaling inputs.
evidence: The text summarizes the main conclusion of the study.

claim: The ability to directionally control rapid changes in daughter fates, and to establish sharp tissue boundaries without the need for direct competition and/or elimination, offers basic advantages to this mechanism that are likely to be broadly applicable in development.
source: Overall, the ability to directionally control rapid changes in daughter fates, and to establish sharp tissue boundaries without the need for direct competition and/or elimination, offers basic advantages to this mechanism that are likely to be broadly applicable in development.
evidence: The text provides speculation about the broader implications of the findings.

claim: The first of three spatially positioned arrays of hair placodes emerges when some cells within an epithelial monolayer begin to experience a higher level of WNT signal than their neighbors.
source: During embryonic development, the first of three spatially positioned arrays of hair placodes emerges when some cells within an epithelial monolayer begin to experience a higher level of WNT signal than their neighbors (DasGupta and Fuchs, 1999).
evidence: The text cites previous literature (DasGupta and Fuchs, 1999) to support this claim.

claim: WNTs act as short-range inducers and long-range organizers in hair follicle development, similar to Drosophila development.
source: Similar to Drosophila development, these WNTs act as short-range inducers and long-range organizers.
evidence: The text draws a comparison to Drosophila development.

claim: Through either rapid reaction-diffusion or mechanotransduction-mediated mesenchymal self-organization, the WNThi cells within the plane of homogeneous epidermal cells cluster into an array of evenly spaced placodes.
source: Thus, through either rapid reaction-diffusion (Sick et al., 2006; Glover et al., 2017) or mechanotransduction-mediated mesenchymal self-organization (Shyer et al., 2017), the WNThi cells within the plane of homogeneous epidermal cells cluster into an array of evenly spaced placodes (Ahtiainen et al., 2014).
evidence: The text cites previous literature (Sick et al., 2006; Glover et al., 2017; Shyer et al., 2017; Ahtiainen et al., 2014) to support this claim.

claim: As placodes form, they produce inhibitory signals such as bone morphogenic proteins (BMPs) that limit placode size and distance placodes from each other.
source: As placodes form, they produce inhibitory signals such as bone morphogenic proteins (BMPs) that limit placode size and distance placodes from each other (Narhi et al., 2008; Noramly and Morgan, 1998).
evidence: The text cites previous literature (Narhi et al., 2008; Noramly and Morgan, 1998) to support this claim.

claim: Three dimensional pattern formation begins when WNT signaling reaches a threshold in placode cells, stimulating them to divide perpendicularly relative to the epidermal plane and generating differentially fated progenitor daughters.
source: Three dimensional pattern formation begins when WNT signaling reaches a threshold in placode cells, stimulating them to divide perpendicularly relative to the epidermal plane and generating differentially fated progenitor daughters (Ouspenskaia et al., 2016).
evidence: The text cites previous literature (Ouspenskaia et al., 2016) to support this claim.

claim: Early basal daughters both produce WNTs and respond to WNTs, as exemplified by WNT-reporter activity and nuclear LEF1.
source: Intriguingly, these early basal daughters both produce WNTs and respond to WNTs, as exemplified by WNT-reporter activity and nuclear LEF1, a positive-acting downstream DNA binding effector of WNT-stabilized β-catenin (Figure 1A; Ouspenskaia et al., 2016).

claim: In the Drosophila wing margin, cells closer to the dorsoventral boundary repress wingless expression in their juxtaposed neighbors through a self-refining mechanism involving NOTCH.
source: A similar refining mechanism has been previously proposed in the Drosophila imaginal disks. In the wingless expressing cells of the wing margin, cells that are closer to the dorsoventral boundary are able to repress wingless expression in their juxtaposed neighbors through a self-refining mechanism. In this case, however, the mechanism appears to involve NOTCH, whose activity is required for wingless expression, which in turn appears to repress NOTCH activity (Rulifson et al., 1996).
